pr_title: Report a diagnostic for return types with HResult-like named structures and provide a code-fix to do the correct marshalling
pr_body:
Many developers use struct based HRESULT types to provide a more helpful API interface on top of HRESULT-based errors. This is technically incorrect per the ABI, but due to prexisting behavior, [we couldn't fix this in bulit-in COM](https://github.com/dotnet/coreclr/pull/23974). In source-generated COM, we fixed this from the outset, but we didn't provide a good way for developers to determine that this change is the cause of runtime failures.

This PR implements a feature where `MarshalAs(UnmanagedType.Error)` on a value type in a COM interface marshals the type as an int at the ABI boundary. We will provide a diagnostic when this may be useful and a code fix to add the attribute. Additionally, we also enlighten the "Convert to source-generated COM" fixer to add the attribute when it is likely to be helpful.

Fixes #89603

> LGTM, my only other thought is if we want to add a warning that the struct should be 4 bytes for the bitcast

I don't think we need to add a warning here as likely everyone that will use this will have a struct that just has one int field in it. I'd be shocked if anyone used any other HRESULT type shape. A runtime error is fine here I think.

issue_context.title: ComInterfaceGenerator should warn on PreserveSig methods that return a struct named HResult
issue_context.body: Unlike built-in COM, source generated COM is using the `MemberFunction` calling convention. This calling convention is correct for COM, but will cause failures for any code that blindly converts their COM interfaces that also happen to use an HResult struct. We should detect this case and warn the user that they need to define a custom marshaller for their HResult type.

Unlike built-in COM, source generated COM is using the `MemberFunction` calling convention. This calling convention is correct for COM, but will cause failures for any code that blindly converts their COM interfaces that also happen to use an HResult struct. We should detect this case and warn the user that they need to define a custom marshaller for their HResult type.
Author: jkoritzinsky
Assignees: -
Labels: `area-System.Runtime.InteropServices`
Milestone: -

> We should detect this case and warn the user that they need to define a custom marshaller for their HResult type.

I'm not overly thrilled with the following suggestion, but since this pattern is so pervasive perhaps we should have a pre-canned marshaller for this and just apply it?

We could have a predefined marshaller that users could apply, but I'd rather not auto-apply it just to any struct named `HResult`. I'd rather the user have to manually apply it. We could provide a code-fix to enable it.

review_comments: Since this diagnostic only deals with returning HResults and is associated with this Code fixer, should we rename it to something more specific so that we don't add more diagnostics under this ID and make this code fixer deal with a bunch of unrelated diagnostics. Or do you think it won't be a big deal?

It's okay for the fixer to not offer any fixes, so I think it's okay to make this fixer a little more general. The fixer mainly looks at the well-known property name, so the diagnostic ID should be okay. I'm planning on extending it in the future to also be used by `bool`s for their MarshalAs options. I'll update the fixer to gracefully handle other usages of the same diagnostic ID that don't have the property..
